description: Our project is FarmShift a platform that will use NASA satellite data to help farmers make better decisions around rainfall, drought, crop rotation, planting periods, and farm risk.
summary:
MundaLens helps farmers make more informed crop-rotation decisions by combining NASA Earth observation data, historical weather patterns and local soil conditions.

Farmers can select their field using a satellite map, GPS location or coordinates. The system analyses rainfall, temperature, soil characteristics, vegetation and terrain, then compares the current crop with two alternative crop-rotation options.

Using a daily soil-water balance model, MundaLens estimates crop water requirements, water deficits, dry spells and relative yield potential. It also examines historical seasons to assess how different crops may perform under typical and difficult conditions.

Unlike systems that simply display weather information, MundaLens translates environmental observations into understandable agricultural decisions. It aims to help farmers anticipate water-related risks, explore alternative planting strategies and make more resilient decisions in changing climate conditions.

The project supports climate-smart agriculture, improved farm planning and more informed use of Earth observation data, particularly for smallholder farmers.
details:
How MundaLens Works

MundaLens is a web-based agricultural decision-support system designed to help farmers evaluate crop-rotation options using satellite observations, weather history and soil characteristics.

1. Farm Identification

Farmers can select their field through an interactive satellite map, use their device location with permission, search for a location or manually enter geographical coordinates. The selected coordinates determine the environmental data retrieved for the farm.

2. NASA Earth Observation Integration

The application integrates several NASA resources:

  • NASA POWER provides historical daily rainfall, maximum and minimum temperatures, humidity, wind speed and solar radiation.
  • GPM IMERG provides precipitation imagery and supports daily rainfall analysis where authenticated data access is configured.
  • SMAP provides root-zone soil moisture observations where NASA Earthdata access is configured.
  • Landsat/Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 observations provide vegetation information through the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI).
  • SRTM provides elevation and terrain slope information.

3. Soil and Environmental Analysis

MundaLens retrieves soil texture, water-holding capacity and pH information using SoilGrids. Terrain slope is considered when estimating how much rainfall infiltrates the soil rather than contributing to runoff.

4. Crop Rotation Intelligence

The application compares the farmer's current crop against two alternative crop-rotation scenarios. It simulates daily soil-water availability, crop water demand, rainfall effectiveness and water stress throughout crop growth stages.

Reference evapotranspiration is calculated using the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith method when sufficient weather inputs are available, with the Hargreaves method as a fallback.

5. Historical Risk Assessment

The model replays comparable seasonal periods across previous years, where sufficient historical data is available. It evaluates median and difficult-year outcomes to avoid relying on a single season.

6. Decision Support

Farmers receive crop rankings, rotation comparisons, estimated water deficits, relative yield indicators, dry-spell information and confidence assessments. The application also provides optional farmer-entered market scenarios to compare potential gross margins.

Technologies Used

  • Python for the analytical engine and backend.
  • FastAPI for application APIs.
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the frontend.
  • Leaflet for interactive mapping.
  • NumPy for numerical computation.
  • Rasterio, h5py and netCDF4 for geospatial and satellite data processing.
  • NASA Earthdata services and APIs for Earth observation access.

Innovation and Impact

The main innovation is connecting multiple environmental datasets to a practical crop-rotation decision process. Instead of simply showing satellite images or weather forecasts, MundaLens attempts to explain what environmental conditions mean for alternative planting decisions.

The intended impact is to support climate-resilient agriculture, improve seasonal planning, reduce exposure to water-related crop risks and make Earth observation information more accessible to farmers.

Limitations and Future Development

The model uses approximate crop parameters and should be locally calibrated against observed yields, crop varieties and planting calendars. Some numerical satellite products require NASA Earthdata authentication. Recommendations are preliminary decision-support estimates and should be validated against local agronomic knowledge and field observations.
